candidates.explanation: Best guess; the body is elided in the snippet so I could not confirm it. The service passes {id, hash} as conditions so a refresh only succeeds when the presented hash matches the stored one. If the update(...) call filters only on id and ignores conditions.hash, a stale refresh token still affects a row and a new token pair is issued on every replay.

Same risk in the Mongo implementation, whose body is also elided. If the findOneAndUpdate filter uses only the id and omits the hash, an old refresh token still matches the session and rotates it again.

Rotation relies entirely on updateByHash enforcing the hash match, with no separate check here. The code as shown looks correct, but if the repository does not enforce the hash, nothing else rejects a replayed token.

fix.description: Make the update conditional on both id and hash. In the relational repository call this.sessionRepository.update({ id: Number(conditions.id), hash: conditions.hash }, payload). In the Mongo repository use the filter { _id: conditions.id, hash: conditions.hash }. A stale hash then affects no rows and returns null, so refreshToken throws UnauthorizedException.
